60346.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
60346.question_text: When Paul and Barnabas healed a cripple at Lystra, the people named them
60346.explanation:
When Paul and Barnabas healed a cripple at Lystra, the people named them Zeus and Hermes. This incident is recorded in Acts 14:8-12 (RSV):

8 Now at Lystra there was a man sitting, who could not use his feet; he was a cripple from birth, who had never walked. 9 He listened to Paul speaking; and Paul, looking intently at him and seeing that he had faith to be made well, 10 said in a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” And he sprang up and walked. 11 And when the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in Lycao′nian, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!” 12 Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul, because he was the chief speaker, they called Hermes.

60426.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
60426.question_text: Pilate delivered Jesus to be crucified because he
60426.explanation: Pilate's decision to deliver Jesus to be crucified was largely influenced by the pressure from the crowd. The chief priests and elders, who stirred up the crowd, demanded Jesus' crucifixion, and Pilate, wanting to maintain order and avoid a potential riot, yielded to their demands. Pilate himself found no fault in Jesus and even washed his hands publicly to symbolize his innocence in the matter, but he ultimately chose to prioritize political expediency and placating the crowd over justice.

60455.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
60455.question_text: On arrival in Rome, Paul first addressed
60455.explanation: When Paul arrived in Rome, he was placed under house arrest but was allowed to meet people freely. The first group he addressed was the Jewish leaders (Council) in Rome (Acts 28:17-20). He explained why he was imprisoned and reassured them that he had not come to accuse his fellow Jews but to testify about the hope of Israel (Jesus Christ).
